assessment:
Three wishes, and they do not overlap. Know which one you are holding before you decide what is missing.

Reach first. Enlightened Tutor takes an artifact or an enchantment. Worldly Tutor takes any creature. Sarkhan's Triumph takes a Dragon creature card and nothing else — so it cannot find a cost reducer at all. The four in the 99 besides the commander are Urza's Incubator, Herald's Horn, Dragonspeaker Shaman and Dragonlord's Servant: two artifacts and two non-Dragon bodies. Enlightened Tutor reaches the two artifacts, Worldly Tutor reaches the two bodies, Sarkhan's Triumph reaches none. You draw a reducer by turn six in 41.9% of games (◆ goldfish, 10,000 seeded iterations), so which tutor is in your hand decides whether that hole is fixable at all.

Delivery second. Sarkhan's Triumph puts the card in your hand. The other two shuffle and put it on top, so they cost you a draw step: cast them at the end of the turn before yours and collect the card on your own draw. Cast one on your own turn and you have paid a full rotation for nothing.

Two cards delete that wait, and only for Dragons. Korlessa, Scale Singer lets you cast Dragon spells off the top. Herald's Horn, with Dragon chosen, hands you a topped Dragon creature card on your upkeep. Neither sees Urza's Incubator, Panharmonicon or Chromatic Lantern. Neither sees Dragonspeaker Shaman or Dragonlord's Servant either — a Human and a Goblin. One card in the 99 is both an artifact and a Dragon creature card, and so is the only Enlightened Tutor target either shortcut can see: Moltensteel Dragon.

Colour third. Worldly Tutor asks {G}, at 81.0% on curve from lands alone. Enlightened Tutor asks {W} at 59.2%. Sarkhan's Triumph asks {2}{R} at 51.5%. Rocks and dorks lift those to 91.8%, 81.0% and 74.2% (◆ mana-analysis). The one-mana tutors are also the ones you can hold up on a turn you are already doing something.

Now the change you have to absorb. This deck has no verified win line. Aggravated Assault left the 99 on the v1.0.0 baseline; stacks 003 and 006 both name it and stack 004 names Blasphemous Act and Savage Ventmaw, and all three are held back as boards this list can no longer make. Three checker-passed stacks remain that it can make — 001, 002 and 005 — and they are the only lines here you may treat as proven. The deck declares two kills and its own targets file labels both UNVERIFIED in their titles: the entry kill assembles by turn six in 35.6% of games, the combat kill in 29.0% (◆ goldfish). Point a wish at either. Do not tell yourself you are fetching an infinite. There is not one.

Last, the funding rule, which is narrower than the one you learned. Klauth's attack trigger says spend this mana only to cast spells, so it pays for a tutor. The other four restricted sources are narrower and pay for none of them: Desolation of Smaug and Sarkhan, Fireblood make Dragon-spells-only mana, Maelstrom of the Spirit Dragon makes Dragon-or-Omen mana, and Unclaimed Territory makes creature-spell-of-the-chosen-type mana. A tutor is an instant. And none of the five pays Sneak Attack's {R}, because that is an activated ability rather than a spell — count unrestricted red before you plan the turn.

targets.scenario: Turn two or three, at the end of the turn before yours. Two or three lands down, and nothing in your hand costs less than four.
targets.why: Buy the discount before you buy anything else. You draw one of the four cost reducers by turn six in 41.9% of games, mean turn 3.28 when you get one (◆ goldfish) — so in 58.1% of games you do not have one, and this is the wish that fixes the hand you were actually dealt. Incubator takes {2} off every Dragon creature spell and stacks with eminence's {1}, so your six-drops cost three and The Ur-Dragon drops from nine to seven. Take Herald's Horn instead when your hand is empty rather than heavy: {1} less, and its upkeep look feeds you Dragons you have not drawn yet. ★

targets.scenario: Mid-game, four or five lands on the battlefield and the wrong ones. You are holding Crux of Fate or Dragonlord Kolaghan with no black source, or Miirym with two of her three colours.
targets.why: Fetch the fixing, not the payoff. Only three cards in the 99 ask for black — the commander, Crux of Fate and Dragonlord Kolaghan — and black is the lowest of the five on curve: 21.7% from lands alone and 52.4% once rocks and dorks are counted, against 51.5% for red, 59.2% for white and blue, and 81.0% for green (◆ mana-analysis). Fourteen of 31 lands enter tapped. Lantern gives every land you already control 'add one mana of any color', so it repairs the board in front of you instead of the board you might draw. The pilot's own reading of game 001 was that mana consistency is the bottleneck rather than card selection; this is the wish that acts on that. ★

targets.scenario: A per-Dragon payoff is already down — Dragon Tempest, Terror of the Peaks or Scourge of Valkas — and your hand holds a Dragon you cannot pay for.
targets.why: Stop paying for Dragons and start renting them. Stack 005 priced it exactly: {R} puts Drakuseth, Maw of Flames onto the battlefield with haste, the attack trigger deals 4 and 3 and 3 before blockers, it connects for 7 in the air, and all 17 damage stands after the mandatory end-step sacrifice (✓ rules-verified). It is an enchantment, so land it before the sweeper rather than after. One warning that comes from your mana rather than the card: the {R} is an activated ability, and none of Desolation of Smaug, Klauth, Maelstrom of the Spirit Dragon, Sarkhan, Fireblood or Unclaimed Territory can pay for it.

targets.scenario: Miirym, Sentinel Wyrm has survived a rotation, Terror of the Peaks or Dragon Tempest is down, and you still hold a nontoken Dragon.
targets.why: Stack 002 resolved that board. One Lathliss cast produced two nonlegendary Lathliss copies — Panharmonicon doubles Miirym's trigger — and 64 damage in twelve separately targeted instances, killing a 32-life opponent outright while a 40-life opponent survived at 8 (✓ rules-verified). Cast the artifact on a quiet turn and hold the Dragon for the loud one; nobody prices a four-mana artifact as a kill until it has been one. Know why it stops at two copies before you count on a bigger number: the copies are tokens, and the 'nontoken' clause on Miirym and on every Lathliss skips them.

tutors.notes: One white mana at instant speed, and the card goes on TOP — cast it at the end of the turn before yours so your own draw step collects it. Nothing in this deck shortcuts that wait for an artifact or an enchantment: Korlessa casts Dragon spells off the top and Herald's Horn peeks for Dragon creature cards, and the only artifact in the 99 either one can see is Moltensteel Dragon, which is not on this sheet. The search is revealed, so treat casting it as an announcement. Reveal Sneak Attack two turns before you use it and you have told the table which permanent to kill.

targets.scenario: Turn six or later, at an opponent's end step. You will have five mana next turn, the commander is still in the command zone, and the table has stopped watching your combat step.
targets.why: Rent the commander instead of buying him. The Ur-Dragon has a mean cast turn of 8.172 and arrives by turn six in 4.1% of games; in 7,170 of 10,000 he never arrives by turn ten at all (◆ goldfish). Courser costs {4}{R}{R}, five with eminence, and his entry puts The Ur-Dragon onto the battlefield with haste — so you attack, draw a card for each attacking Dragon, and put a permanent from hand onto the battlefield, and he returns to the command zone at end step with no tax accrued. Fetch at their end step, cast on yours, attack the same turn.

targets.scenario: Dragon Tempest is on the battlefield, you can reach seven mana next turn including {W}{W}, and one opponent has no flying blocker.
targets.why: This is the deck's one contained combo line and it has a stack behind it. Ancient Gold Dragon costs {5}{W}{W}, six with eminence; connect once and the d20 makes that many 1/1 flying Faerie Dragons at the same time. Stack 001 fixed the roll at 15 and resolved the cascade: Dragon Tempest triggers fifteen times, each trigger dealt X = 17 on that board of two other Dragons, and the 30-life opponent died to the second trigger aimed at them (✓ rules-verified). Two findings from that stack to plan around. Miirym does not copy the tokens, because they are tokens. And every trigger locks its target when it goes on the stack, so triggers aimed at a player who has already left the game fizzle — spread them rather than stacking them on one seat. Note the cost: {W}{W} on a deck at 59.2% white on curve from lands alone (◆ mana-analysis), so check the sources before you fetch.

targets.scenario: Two or three Dragons already attacking, and no way to make the swing lethal this turn.
targets.why: Take the multiplier rather than another body. Thrakkus costs {3}{R}{G}, four with eminence, and doubles the power of each Dragon you control when he attacks — a pair of 5/5 Dragon tokens swings as 10/5s. This is one half of what the targets file calls THE COMBAT KILL, and that file labels it UNVERIFIED in its own title: it assembles by turn six in 29.0% of games and in 41.1% within ten (◆ goldfish). No stack has resolved it, so play it as a clock, not as a kill. Atarka, World Render is the same wish one mana up if double strike suits the board better; Thrakkus is the one you can fetch and cast on the same turn off seven mana.

targets.scenario: Turn five or six, you missed a land drop, and the top of your hand is stranded behind your mana.
targets.why: Fetch mana wearing a Dragon. Rapacious Dragon costs {4}{R}, four with eminence, and makes two Treasures as it enters — unrestricted mana that pays for anything, an activated ability included. Your land drop rate is 52.5% on turn five and 43.1% on turn six (◆ goldfish), so the turn you miss one is a turn to expect rather than to be surprised by. It is also one of only two Treasure sources in the 99 the goldfish can actually spend, the other being Smaug the Magnificent's upkeep trigger — you hold some Treasure source by turn six in 61.8% of games across all seven, but five of the seven are gated on combat or on an opponent's choice, which is why every Treasure-derived mana figure here is a floor (◆ goldfish).

tutors.notes: The only tutor here that puts the card in your HAND — no transit turn, no draw step spent — so this is the one you cast on the turn you need the card, and the one to keep for the piece you cannot afford to telegraph a turn early. It pays for that with reach: Dragon creature cards only. No Sneak Attack, no Panharmonicon, no land, and none of the four cost reducers, since Urza's Incubator and Herald's Horn are artifacts while Dragonspeaker Shaman is a Human and Dragonlord's Servant a Goblin. It is also the most expensive of the three at {2}{R}, on the colour that runs 51.5% on curve from lands alone (◆ mana-analysis). Three mana at instant speed still means you shop on somebody else's end step and keep your whole turn to cast what you found.

targets.scenario: Turn one or two with a green source open. Your keep was two lands and a fistful of five-drops, with no reducer and no rock.
targets.why: Fetch the discount in the one place Enlightened Tutor cannot reach it. Dragonspeaker Shaman costs {1}{R}{R} and takes {2} off every Dragon spell — the same discount as Urza's Incubator, one mana cheaper and a turn earlier. You hold a reducer by turn six in 41.9% of games and a reducer plus ramp in only 28.5% (◆ goldfish), and that second number is the hand that casts a Dragon on curve. Take Dragonlord's Servant instead when you will only have two mana next turn: {1}{R}, {1} off, on the board a turn sooner. Neither is a Dragon, so Korlessa and Herald's Horn will not shortcut the top of your library here and the transit turn is real.

targets.scenario: Turn two or three, one green open, and you are holding your other topping tutor or expect to draw into one.
targets.why: Buy the card that makes your topping tutors free. Korlessa costs {G}{U} — eminence cannot cut it, since there is no generic mana in that cost to cut — and she lets you cast Dragon spells straight off the top of your library. From then on a Worldly Tutor aimed at a Dragon costs no draw step at all: shuffle, put it on top, cast it off the top on your turn. She does nothing for Enlightened Tutor, whose targets are artifacts and enchantments with Moltensteel Dragon the one exception, and Sarkhan's Triumph never needed her. She also turns the top card into information you keep for the rest of the game, which is what makes a shuffle-then-top tutor safe to cast into a board you have not read yet. ★

targets.scenario: Mid-game with five mana and three colours available. Terror of the Peaks or Dragon Tempest is already down and your hand still holds nontoken Dragons.
targets.why: Fetch the doubler before you fetch a body, because everything after her arrives twice. Every nontoken Dragon you cast brings a token copy, and stack 002 resolved what that is worth beside Panharmonicon: one Lathliss cast, two Lathliss copies, 64 damage in twelve targeted instances (✓ rules-verified). She costs {3}{G}{U}{R}, five with eminence, which is three colours on a deck where green is 81.0% on curve from lands alone and blue 59.2% (◆ mana-analysis) — check the second colour before you fetch, not after. She is a Dragon Spirit, so with Korlessa out you cast her off the top and lose no turn. Ward {2} is why she survives the rotation you need her to survive.

targets.scenario: Sneak Attack is on the battlefield, you have {R} plus one green, and you need damage this turn rather than a board next turn.
targets.why: One green mana turns a dead draw step into stack 005's line: Drakuseth on top, {R} to put him in with haste, 4 and 3 and 3 from the attack trigger before blockers, 7 more in the air, and all 17 damage standing after the end-step sacrifice (✓ rules-verified). Pick the three targets before you activate rather than after — the trigger locks them when it goes on the stack. Without Sneak Attack he is {4}{R}{R}{R}, six with eminence, and mean available mana is 4.669 on turn six and 5.428 on turn eight (◆ goldfish), so hard-casting him is a late-game plan and Sneak Attack is what makes him a turn-five one.

tutors.notes: One green mana — tied with Enlightened Tutor for the cheapest of the three — and the widest inside its type: any creature card, which is the only route to the two cost reducers that are not artifacts. {G} is the most reliable of the five colours at 81.0% on curve from lands alone and 91.8% with rocks and dorks (◆ mana-analysis), so this is the tutor you can hold up on a turn you are also casting something. It puts the card on top, so cast it at the end of the turn before yours. With Korlessa out that wait disappears for a Dragon, and Herald's Horn's upkeep trigger pulls a topped Dragon creature card into your hand for nothing — neither helps for Dragonspeaker Shaman or Dragonlord's Servant.

gaps: There is no infinite left to fetch. Aggravated Assault left the 99 with the v1.0.0 baseline and took the deck's only checker-verified win line with it: stacks 003 and 006 name it, stack 004 names Blasphemous Act and Savage Ventmaw, and all three are marked not presentable — the verdicts stand, the boards cannot be built. Stacks 001, 002 and 005 are what remain. If you catch yourself spending a wish 'on the combo', you are working from the old sheet.

Both of the deck's declared kills are unverified, and this guide points wishes at them anyway. THE ENTRY KILL assembles by turn six in 35.6% of games and THE COMBAT KILL in 29.0% (◆ goldfish); goldfish_targets.json labels both UNVERIFIED in their own titles because no stack has resolved either. A resolve-stack run on Thrakkus or Atarka doubling an attacking Dragon board, or on Utvara Hellkite making a token per attacker underneath a per-Dragon payoff, would settle the combat half.

No wish reaches the graveyard. Patriarch's Bidding left the 99 on the same baseline, so nothing here rebuys a Dragon that has died and nothing at all recovers one that has been exiled. Play around exile removal rather than planning to answer it.

Maelstrom of the Spirit Dragon is a fourth search this guide does not cover: {4}, {T}, sacrifice it, find a Dragon card and put it into your hand. It is a land, so it belongs to the mana analysis rather than to this sheet — but price it before you rely on it, because it costs four mana plus the land itself, and unlike Fabled Passage it puts no land back — it is the one search here that costs you a permanent outright.

No wish here answers a mana-denial permanent, and that is a choice rather than an oversight. After game 001 the pilot declined to build around Blood Moon and named it an accepted risk at bracket 3+, so the Chromatic Lantern wish above is sized against the deck's own colour maths — black at 21.7% on curve from lands alone, 14 of 31 lands entering tapped — and not against that card.

The goldfish figures quoted here for Treasure and for combat are floors. Five of the seven Treasure sources and five combat effects are unreadable to the model and are named in goldfish_metrics.json's meta block, so a wish sized on those rates is sized on a lower bound. The colour figures from mana-analysis carry the opposite caveat: Desolation of Smaug and Sarkhan, Fireblood add mana that manabase counts as zero sources, which is right for colour maths and wrong for 'can I cast my commander' — that mana is drawn by turn six in 23.6% of games (◆ goldfish) and is tracked as its own target for exactly that reason.
